chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said:
I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) one day, and a stuffed chicken, prepared as khabeeص (a type of sweet dough/confection), was brought to us. We broke it apart and ate it.
Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdul A'ala, who said:
I ate with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) – like the first report.

key_terms.خَبِيصاً: khabeeص (a type of sweet dough or confection)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating stuffed chicken in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the permissibility of *khabeeص* (a sweet dough or confection) and stuffed poultry, illustrating the Imam’s enjoyment of rich, festive foods. It serves as a practical precedent for culinary traditions in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that such delicacies are not only permissible but can be sources of pleasure when consumed in moderation.
